clue.text: Professional US magazine highly esteemed, grew rapidly

parts.note: a professional is a pro
Life is a famous American photo magazine
something highly esteemed is well rated

explanation.surface: A professional American magazine, much admired, expanded fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply or spread quickly, a synonym for growing rapidly.

clue.text: What tells you to stop getting led astray — with proper protection

indicators.note: the word for proper surrounds the rearranged letters, protecting them

parts.note: proper means right or correct

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to stop being misled, with suitable safeguards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What tells you to stop' is a traffic signal, not a person; 'astray' scrambles EDL, which the 'protection' wraps after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic signal at red instructs drivers to halt.

clue.text: See promotion offering lots

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
an ad is a promotion or advertisement

explanation.surface: Look at an advert with lots of things on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A load, informally, means a great deal or plenty.

clue.text: I rant terribly when sat on by police? Definitely

indicators.note: in a down clue the police word sits on top of the jumbled letters

parts.note: a police force

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters of I rant are jumbled

explanation.surface: I rant badly when the police sit on me? Absolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so 'for certain' means it is beyond doubt, the idiom matching definitely.

clue.text: Artist gets disease — it must be something eaten

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: A painter gets gout and blames something he ate.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a rich meat stew, so it is a dish that is eaten.

clue.text: Cheaper attire falling apart after short time

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: falling apart means disintegrating, so the letters of attire are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheap clothes come apart after a little while.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby or cheap-looking, so the comparative fits cheaper.

clue.text: Greediest man involved in quarrel

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of greediest man are mixed

explanation.surface: The greediest man gets caught up in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is an argument or dispute between people.

clue.text: Part of speech in which nothing initially is ruled out

indicators.note: the opening letter is struck off, being the one at the start

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A part of speech where nothing is excluded at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' reads as grammar, but 'Part' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is an allotted portion or share, so it is a part.

clue.text: District gets prize, but not the first one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for prize is dropped

parts.note: an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A local area wins an award, though not the top one.
explanation.definitionFit: An electoral district of a city or borough is called a ward.

clue.text: Claims of Yorkshire town in need of hotel

indicators.note: lacking or needing the letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: belonging to the Yorkshire spa town of Harrogate, so the possessive Harrogate's
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Insurance claims from a Yorkshire town that needs a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROGATE is a spa town in North Yorkshire; 'of' makes it possessive, HARROGATE'S, and 'in need of' hotel removes its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize something without right, so this verb form matches 'claims'.

clue.text: Army capturing Greek character with 21 suffering put in 9?

indicators.note: the army word holds the Greek letter inside

parts.note: a host is an army or multitude
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: suffering means distressed, so the letters of 21's answer are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 21 down, a word for models

explanation.surface: An army takes a Greek with suffering principles and puts him in a district.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is the answer to 9 across, a hospital ward; 'suffering' makes ALISED from the answer to 21.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient admitted to a hospital ward has been placed in one.

clue.text: Start with nothing at home — get equipment installed

indicators.note: the equipment is fitted inside the other letters

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
someone at home is in
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Begin with an empty house and have the kit put in.
explanation.definitionFit: A start or source of something is its origin; both nouns mean the beginning.

clue.text: Reading University agent about to spill the beans

indicators.note: the word for agent is turned round

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
to sing is slang for confessing or informing

explanation.surface: A Reading University agent is on the point of revealing secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' at the start poses as the Berkshire town and its university; it is the definition, a present participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Perusing a text is reading it carefully, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Tiny worker, one going round in circles

parts.note: minute means tiny
a hand is a worker, as on a farm

explanation.surface: A tiny employee goes round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: The long pointer on a clock face sweeps round once an hour, endlessly circling.

clue.text: Criticise this set, unorthodox believers in divine nature?

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: unorthodox means irregular, so the letters of this set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Critics savage a group with unconventional religious views.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism identifies God with the natural universe, so its followers believe nature itself is divine.

clue.text: Language to get rid of when seen as heartless

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed, as if its heart were cut out

parts.note: to erase is to get rid of or wipe out

explanation.surface: A language one wants rid of because it seems unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Cold girl — one starts to beguile all lovers as man-eater

parts.note: C is cold, as on a tap
Ann is a girl's name
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A cold woman sets out to charm every admirer as a man-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man-eater' suggests a predatory woman, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal literally eats human flesh.

clue.text: Uninspiring side, second to finish

indicators.note: the second letter of the word for side is sent to the end

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A dull team that came second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to finish' moves TEAM's second letter, E, to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame can mean dull or lacking excitement, so it fits uninspiring.

clue.text: Servants providing repasts around Belfast etc.

indicators.note: the meals word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: repasts are meals
Belfast and its surroundings are in NI, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Servants serving dinners in and around Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Menials are servants who do lowly domestic work.

clue.text: Saint troubled when joining in religious feast, showing dislike of ceremony

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the feast

parts.note: Purim is a Jewish festival

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of saint are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disturbed saint at a religious festival shows his distaste for ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: Purim is the Jewish festival recalling Esther; 'troubled' gives TANIS, and 'joining in' sets it before the feast's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritans rejected elaborate ritual in worship, so their creed is marked by aversion to ceremony.

clue.text: More than one model is accepting contract

indicators.note: the word is takes the contract word inside it

parts.note: a deal is a contract

explanation.surface: More than one fashion model is taking a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect examples to follow, models in the plural.

clue.text: Volume repeatedly deficient? That's a mistake

indicators.note: the shortened word is given twice
lacking, so the last letter is missing

parts.note: a volume is a book

explanation.surface: A book that is twice found lacking is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A booboo is an informal word for a silly blunder.

clue.text: River traversed by solitary person who lives near the Thames?

definitions.text: person who lives near the Thames?

indicators.note: the river runs across the inside of the word for solitary

parts.note: a solitary, as a noun, is a loner or recluse
the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A river crossed by a lone figure living beside the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: London stands on the Thames, so one of its residents is a fair cryptic hint for a city dweller there.

clue.text: One of the unpaid trainees? Bury has any number

parts.note: to inter is to bury
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An unpaid trainee from Bury, the Lancashire town, has any number of jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' with its capital looks like the Lancashire town; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a trainee, often unpaid, doing work experience.

clue.text: Deity offering bold sign oddly missed

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are left out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A god displaying a bold symbol, oddly missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Celebrity, showing no interest, we hear? That's right

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken and a same-sounding spelling is used

parts.note: someone showing no interest is bored

explanation.surface: A famous person, apparently bored, is told they are right.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel facing forward.

clue.text: Old measure established by British inventor

parts.note: an ell is an old unit of length for cloth

explanation.surface: An old unit of measurement was set up by a British inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old measure' looks like the definition (a bel is a unit), but it is the ell; 'established by' puts B before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell, the Scottish-born inventor, is credited with the telephone.

clue.text: Troubled Penny toddles around, showing hope is lost?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of penny toddles are mixed up

explanation.surface: An upset Penny wanders about looking hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondency is a state of having lost hope, so acting this way shows hopelessness.
